name: Pac-Man
loop: Eat every dot in the maze while four ghosts with distinct AI chase you; power pellets turn the tables.
pitch: The benchmark. Championship Edition (2007) and CE2 proved the formula: neon, speed ramps, ghost trains, pulsing music. Worth studying before building anything else.
modern: Pac-Man Championship Edition DX / CE2, Pac-Man 99

name: Boulder Dash
loop: Dig through dirt collecting diamonds before time runs out, while boulders and gems fall under cellular-automaton physics.
pitch: Grid physics that plays perfectly in 3D: chunky dirt with volumetric crumble, rolling boulders with real weight, dynamic lighting from glowing diamonds, amoeba as animated goo. Rules are tiny and fully deterministic.
modern: Boulder Dash 30th Anniversary (2014) — pleasant but flat; room for a truly premium take
adds: Shared Godot core, grid engine, level packs + BDCFF, editor, procedural Blender props, glow and particles, jsfxr sound, MIDI music, AI capture and test loop.

name: Cannon Fodder
loop: Guide a tiny squad with mouse clicks: left to move, right to shoot; grenades and rockets for buildings; recruits die permanently.
pitch: Top-down diorama style (tilt-shift miniature look) fits perfectly: little soldiers on lush jungle, snow and desert terrain, destructible huts, water shaders, and the famous graveyard hill between missions.
modern: Cannon Fodder 3 (2011, poorly received) — the space is open
adds: Top-down 3D terrain, squads, pathfinding, destructibles, vehicles, first binary map importer.

name: Qix
loop: Draw lines to claim 75% of the board while the Qix — an abstract swirling line creature — and Sparx try to kill you.
pitch: Extremely simple and hypnotic. The Qix becomes a gorgeous GPU ribbon/plasma entity; claimed areas reveal a picture or a 3D scene. Perfect for a Tetris Effect–style audiovisual treatment.
modern: Volfied, Gals Panic lineage — no premium modern version

name: Alley Cat
loop: A stray cat leaps between fences, trash cans and clotheslines, jumps through open windows into mini-rooms (fishbowl, mice in cheese, sleeping dogs) to win the heart of a lady cat.
pitch: Great charm potential: a moonlit city alley with warm window light, furry cat animation, and each window room a tiny handcrafted diorama. Short, well-bounded mini-games.
adds: Platformer physics, a character with many animations, multiple scenes, 2.5D camera.

name: Lemmings
loop: Assign skills (dig, build, block, float…) to mindless lemmings so enough of them reach the exit.
pitch: Destructible terrain + hundreds of tiny animated characters = stunning in a modern stylized 3D world. Level format is simple; the originals' level design is legendary.
modern: Lemmings (PSP/PS4 remakes, mobile F2P) — the PSP one was good, now long gone

name: Bomberman / Dyna Blaster
loop: Drop bombs in a grid arena to blast walls and enemies (or friends), collecting range and bomb-count power-ups.
pitch: Explosions are where modern VFX shines. Local multiplayer makes it the best 'show it to friends' remake. Grid logic is trivial.
modern: Super Bomberman R (2017) — the series is alive, so differentiate with style

name: Arkanoid
loop: Bounce a ball off your paddle (the Vaus) to break bricks, catching capsules for laser, catch, multi-ball.
pitch: Ideal first project: tiny ruleset, instant feedback. Glass/metal bricks with physics shatter, bloom, reactive music. Great test for the whole AI + Blender pipeline.

name: Frogger
loop: Hop a frog across a busy road and a river of logs and turtles to reach home slots.
pitch: Crossy Road proved the diorama/voxel look sells this loop. A photoreal-miniature or claymation style would feel fresh.
modern: Crossy Road (spiritual), Frogger in Toy Town

name: Dig Dug
loop: Tunnel underground, inflate monsters with a pump or crush them with dropped rocks.
pitch: Cross-section of layered earth with parallax and soft-body inflating monsters. Close cousin of Boulder Dash — reuse tech.
modern: Dig Dug Digital (unreleased-ish), Namco Museum ports

name: Pengo
loop: A penguin slides ice blocks to crush Sno-Bees in a maze of ice.
pitch: Ice = refraction, subsurface, crisp reflections; sliding blocks with satisfying impacts. Very under-exploited IP-style concept.

name: Bubble Bobble
loop: Two dragons trap enemies in bubbles and pop them across 100 single-screen levels.
pitch: Soap bubble shaders (iridescence) and cute characters; co-op. Single-screen levels are perfect for handcrafted 3D.

name: Rick Dangerous
loop: Indiana Jones–style explorer avoiding traps in temples, using a pistol, dynamite and a stick.
pitch: Trap-heavy rooms lend themselves to cinematic lighting (torches, dust, collapsing stones). Strong European nostalgia.

name: Lode Runner
loop: Collect gold, dig holes to trap guards; guards respawn and holes refill.
pitch: Clean grid ruleset, 150 original levels, built-in editor tradition. A level editor + sharing could be a killer feature.

name: Sokoban
loop: Push crates onto targets in a warehouse; you can only push, never pull.
pitch: The simplest possible logic; all value is in presentation, feel and level curation. Thousands of free community levels.

name: Chuckie Egg
loop: Farmer Harry collects eggs on ladders and platforms while hens roam; a giant duck is released later.
pitch: Farmyard diorama with charming animals — small, very well known in the UK/Europe.

name: Manic Miner
loop: Collect flashing items in 20 surreal single-screen caverns before air runs out.
pitch: Surreal enemies (toilets, penguins, telephones) could become a fantastic art-direction playground.

name: Marble Madness
loop: Roll a marble down isometric obstacle courses against the clock.
pitch: Already 3D in spirit; with modern physics and materials it's pure eye candy. Short: only 6 levels.

name: Super Sprint
loop: Top-down single-screen racing for up to 3 players, collecting wrenches for upgrades.
pitch: Single-screen tracks as detailed miniatures, tilt-shift camera, local multiplayer chaos.

name: Gauntlet
loop: Four heroes battle hordes pouring out of generators through dungeon mazes; food, keys and potions.
pitch: Hordes + dynamic torch lighting = spectacular. 4-player co-op.

name: Paperboy
loop: Ride a bike down a suburban street throwing newspapers to subscribers while avoiding hazards.
pitch: A stylized American suburb with humour everywhere — a great fit for a toy-like 3D look.

name: Xenon 2 Megablast
loop: Vertical shooter through organic alien landscapes, buying upgrades from a shop between stages.
pitch: Biomechanical backgrounds are a showcase for modern shaders. Iconic Bomb the Bass soundtrack vibe.

name: Speedball 2: Brutal Deluxe
loop: Violent futuristic handball in a metal arena; buy and train players between matches.
pitch: Chrome armour, arena lights, crowd — screams for a modern look. Simple physics and match rules.

name: Pipe Mania
loop: Place random pipe pieces to build a route before the flowing liquid (the 'flooz') catches up.
pitch: Fluid simulation and steampunk plumbing. Tiny rules, very polishable.

name: Q*bert
loop: Hop on a pyramid of cubes to change their colours while avoiding Coily and friends.
pitch: Already isometric 3D; cube materials changing colour with nice transitions.

name: Bomb Jack
loop: Float through the air collecting bombs in order in front of world landmarks (pyramids, Greek temple...).
pitch: The backdrops (Sphinx, Acropolis, Neuschwanstein) are made for dramatic 3D scenery with a light, floaty character.

name: Head over Heels
loop: Control two creatures who can combine; explore ~300 isometric rooms solving puzzles.
pitch: Isometric → real-time 3D is a natural step. Bigger scope, a later target.

name: Worms
loop: Turn-based artillery: teams of worms blow each other up on destructible 2D terrain.
pitch: Well served by Team17 already; listed for reference only.

name: Tetris
loop: Rotate and drop falling tetrominoes to clear lines.
pitch: Reference only: Tetris Effect (2018) is the other gold standard for 'same game, transcendent presentation'. Licence is strictly protected.

name: Z
loop: No base building: capture territory flags and every factory, radar and gun in the sector becomes yours. More territory means faster production. Robot armies fight for the map.
pitch: A fast, aggressive RTS with a ton of personality (the sarcastic robots Brad and Allan, cutscenes). Modern tilt-shift battlefields, destructible terrain, great unit animation. Its compact ruleset suits a solo or AI-driven project better than a full RTS.
modern: Z: Steel Soldiers (2001), mobile ports; no premium remake
adds: RTS layer: territory capture, production, unit AI, fog, minimap, Zod Engine maps.

name: Rampart
loop: Build walls from Tetris-like pieces to enclose castles, place cannons inside your territory, bombard ships or rivals, repeat.
pitch: A three-phase loop in one sentence. Modern destruction physics, splashing water and 4-player online play would give it a lot of room to grow. ChatGPT's favourite.
modern: Rampart (GBA/Xbox Live Arcade ports), no real remake

name: North & South
loop: Light strategy map of the American Civil War; battles, train robberies and fort assaults become small action mini-games.
pitch: Lets you ship 5 to 10 tiny mechanics instead of one huge system. Cartoon humour (from Les Tuniques Bleues) suits stylised 3D.

name: The Chaos Engine
loop: Two mercenaries (player or AI) blast through steampunk levels, activating nodes to open the exit.
pitch: Steampunk Victorian art direction; co-op twin-stick is an easy modern control scheme.

name: Syndicate
loop: Control 4 cyborg agents in isometric cyberpunk cities: assassinate, persuade crowds, steal tech, upgrade between missions.
pitch: A Cannon Fodder in a systemic city with civilians, police, cars, panic and neon rain. A spectacular setting for modern lighting.

name: UFO: Enemy Unknown (X-COM)
loop: Global geoscape management plus turn-based squad battles against aliens.
pitch: Legendary but big. Firaxis has already made modern versions, so it's listed for reference.

name: Theme Hospital
loop: Build and run a hospital full of absurd diseases, managing staff, queues and money.
pitch: Great humour, but a large simulation. Two Point Hospital already occupies this niche.

name: Pang
loop: Shoot harpoons upward to split bouncing balloons into smaller ones in front of world landmarks.
pitch: Weekend-sized project. Bouncing jelly spheres and real-world backdrops, like Bomb Jack. Great co-op.

name: Spy vs. Spy
loop: Two spies search rooms for items and booby-trap furniture for each other, on split screen.
pitch: Slapstick trap comedy made for online or couch 1v1. Cartoon-style 3D would shine. The MAD licence is an issue, so you'd make your own spies.

name: Archon
wiki: Archon: The Light and the Dark
loop: Chess-like board of fantasy pieces; a capture triggers a real-time arena duel between the two units.
pitch: Board plus action mini-battles, a clever hybrid. Magical creatures give you a lot to show off in VFX.

name: M.U.L.E.
loop: Four colonists claim land, outfit robot mules for food/energy/ore and trade in real-time auctions.
pitch: An elegant multiplayer economy game. The visuals matter less here; online play is the modern hook.

name: Rod Land
loop: Two fairies with magic rods and rainbow ladders slam enemies around single-screen levels.
pitch: Cute pastel style that toon-shaded 3D would turn into a Nintendo-like look.

name: Fire & Ice
loop: Cool Coyote freezes enemies and collects key pieces through themed worlds.
pitch: Ice-and-fire materials and a charming mascot. Andrew Braybrook's cult classic.

name: The Lost Vikings
loop: Switch between three Vikings with different abilities (run, shield, attack) to solve puzzle levels.
pitch: Great puzzle design with plenty of character. Blizzard owns it (it's in the Blizzard Arcade Collection).

name: Superfrog
loop: A caped frog speeds through Sonic-like levels collecting coins and fruit.
pitch: Colourful mascot platformer, Amiga nostalgia.

name: Scorched Earth
loop: Tanks take turns firing with angle and power across destructible terrain, buying absurd weapons between rounds.
pitch: 'The Mother of All Games'. Destructible voxel terrain plus nukes means huge explosions. Tiny ruleset and a party-game feel.

name: Micro Machines
loop: Tiny toy cars race on breakfast tables, desks and bathtubs; the screen follows the leader.
pitch: Tabletop tracks are a perfect match for realistic-miniature rendering.
modern: Micro Machines World Series (2017, poorly received)

name: Fruity Frank
loop: Frank tunnels through his garden collecting fruit, drops apples on the monsters and throws a bouncing ball to stop them.
pitch: A lush vegetable-garden diorama: soft soil you carve through, glossy fruit, cartoon monsters. Shares its dig-and-crush tech with Boulder Dash and Dig Dug, so it's cheap once one of those exists.
adds: First rigged and animated character, enemy AI in dug tunnels, deformable soil.

name: Double Dragon
loop: Billy and Jimmy Lee fight through a city gang to rescue Marian, with punches, kicks, throws and weapons picked up from enemies.
pitch: Neon-soaked 80s streets, rain, weapon physics and meaty hit-stop. Two-player co-op is the draw. The combat has to feel heavy, which is animation work more than rules work.
modern: Double Dragon Neon (2012), Double Dragon Gaiden (2023)
adds: Melee combat, hit-stop, grabs and throws, weapon physics, co-op.

name: Winter Games
loop: A set of winter sports events (ski jump, biathlon, speed skating, figure skating, hot dog aerials, bobsled), each with its own joystick timing or rhythm control, played in turn by up to 8 players.
pitch: The controls were the fun, so a remake should lean on today's inputs: triggers, gyro aiming, rumble and online play in turn. Snow, ice and alpine lighting are easy wins for modern rendering.
modern: None faithful; Olympic licensed games are a different style
adds: Outdoor snow and ice environments, event framework, analogue, gyro and rumble input, hot-seat multiplayer.
